title: Compact-support site comparison respects compactification calculus
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$. All schemes below are finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], without a separatedness assumption on their structure maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Every morphism $f:X\to Y$ to which compact support is applied is separated and finite type and has a chosen compactification $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,p:\overline X\to Y)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], comparison $C_T=\nu_T^*$ [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], and compact-support candidates $F_f^{e,c}=Rp_{e,*}j_!^e$, $F_f^{p,c}=Rp_{p,*}j_!^p$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Define
$$B_f^c=Rp_{p,*}(e_j)\circ\beta_{p,j_!^e}:C_YF_f^{e,c}\longrightarrow F_f^{p,c}C_X,$$
where $\beta_p$ is the counit-mate direct-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] and $e_j:C_{\overline X}j_!^e\cong j_!^pC_X$ is the adjoint extension-by-zero comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. On $D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, $B_f^c$ is invertible and has the following coherence with the canonical compactification maps. For composable separated finite-type morphisms $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$ with chosen compactifications and compatible composition towers, and for two compactifications $c,c'$ of $f$ with a specified proper refinement, use the refinement comparisons $\rho^{e}_{c',c}:F_f^{e,c}\to F_f^{e,c'}$ and $\rho^p_{c',c}:F_f^{p,c}\to F_f^{p,c'}$, and composition comparisons $\alpha^e_{g,f}:F_g^eF_f^e\to F_{gf}^e$, $\alpha^p_{g,f}:F_g^pF_f^p\to F_{gf}^p$ of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons, thm-sf-comp-composition],
$$B_f^{c'}C_Y(\rho^e_{c',c})=\rho^p_{c',c}C_X\circ B_f^c,$$
$$B_{gf}C_Z(\alpha^e_{g,f})=\alpha^p_{g,f}C_X\circ(F_g^pB_f)\circ(B_gF_f^e).$$
For an open immersion $v:Y'\hookrightarrow Y$ and its Cartesian pullback $u:X'\hookrightarrow X$, let $f':X'\to Y'$ be the pullback and use the pulled-back compactification. The canonical compact-support restriction exchanges $\operatorname{Ex}^e:v_e^*F_f^e\to F_{f'}^eu_e^*$ and $\operatorname{Ex}^p:v_p^*F_f^p\to F_{f'}^pu_p^*$ are invertible and obey
$$\operatorname{Ex}^p\circ v_p^*B_f=B_{f'}u_e^*\circ C_{Y'}(\operatorname{Ex}^e),$$
under the canonical pullback comparisons. All these identities use the normalized proper/open interchanges in compatible compactification towers, including commutative proper/open squares which are not Cartesian, and the counit-mate normalization above; they hold on bounded-below etale witnesses. They respect identities and pasting.

proof.text: Positive-level coefficients are finite. Finite-type schemes over the field are Noetherian by Mathlib LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian and QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace. The bounded-below compact-support comparison is the named natural isomorphism, so each component is invertible.

Expand the bounded-below compact-support comparison into the canonical proper direct-image mate followed by the proper image of the open-extension comparison. Expand properOpenProEtaleIsoPlus into its defining four factors; cancel the first inverse open-extension comparison to obtain the normalized proper/open square. Combine this with the composition equation comparisonDirectImagePlus_comp and naturality of the second proper mate. The etale refinement formula identifies the resulting source composite. This proves the inverse refinement square. Invert the two refinement isomorphisms to obtain the forward square.

Apply the bounded-below square through DerivedCategory.Plus.ι. Expand only compactSupportSiteComparison and compactExchangeTransportComparison to identify their ambient boundary components; cancel the adjacent bounded-below compatibility inverses. This is the square for the actual properTransportRefinement. Apply it to the infFst and infSnd legs of the specified common refinement, invert the first leg, and compose with the second. The etale common-refinement equation identifies the source map with rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationPlusIso.

For chosen compactifications, use the proved originComparison_comp equation defining originComposition. Invert its three boundary isomorphisms, map through the etale-origin inclusion, and identify each inverse originComparison component with compactExchangeTransportComparison. For arbitrary supplied c,d,e, apply the common-refinement change square on the first input, the second input, and the output. Naturality of the second comparison moves the first etale change through it; the adjacent comparison and inverse comparison cancel. Substitution gives exactly coherenceEtaleCompositor and the recorded coherenceProEtaleCompositor. Retain abstract compactification choices through the categorical pasting proof. The public component interfaces evaluate the original canonical four etale and six pro-etale factors with explicit object endpoints; instantiate the abstract calculation only at the end.

The restriction square is the component of compactSupport_exchange_transport. The etale exchange is invertible by compactSupportFiniteTorsion. The actual pro-etale exchange is invertible on the comparison input by isIso_rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationBaseChangeMap_app, using plusEtaleOrigin_mapDerivedCategory_obj.

Induct on CompactSupportSiteDiagram. The preceding refinement, composition and restriction squares prove the three generators. Identity is functoriality. Concatenation substitutes the two induction equations. Push and pull follow from naturality of compactExchangeTransportComparison and leftDerivedUpperStarComparisonIso. For change, use compatibility of the two endpoint isomorphisms to conjugate the induction equation. If two routes have the same etale map, the comparison squares have the same left side; cancel the invertible source boundary to identify the pro-etale routes.

lean.statement: theorem compactSupportSiteCoherence (P : WeilConjectures.PurityFiniteSetting.{u}) : (∀ {X Y : Over (Spec (.of P.field.k))} [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [QuasiCompact X.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType Y.hom] [QuasiCompact Y.hom] (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsSeparated f.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType f.left] [QuasiCompact f.left] (c : Compactification f.left) (L : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf X.left.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} P.Coefficient))), IsIso ((compactSupportSiteComparisonPlus P.Coefficient c).hom.app L)) ∧ (∀ {X X' Y Y' : Over (Spec (.of P.field.k))} [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [QuasiCompact X.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType X'.hom] [QuasiCompact X'.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType Y.hom] [QuasiCompact Y.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType Y'.hom] [QuasiCompact Y'.hom] {f : X ⟶ Y} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {u' : X' ⟶ X} {v : Y' ⟶ Y} [IsSeparated f.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType f.left] [QuasiCompact f.left] [IsOpenImmersion v.left] (sq : IsPullback u'.left f'.left f.left v.left) (c : Compactification f.left) (L : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf X.left.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} P.Coefficient))), IsIso ((Etale.rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationPlusBaseChangeMap P.Coefficient sq c).app L) ∧ IsIso ((rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationBaseChangeMap (ModuleCat.{u + 1} P.Coefficient) sq c).app ((comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} P.Coefficient) X.left).mapDerivedCategory.obj L.obj))) ∧ (∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} {b₀ b₁ : CompactSupportSiteBoundary P.Coefficient T} (D : CompactSupportSiteDiagram P b₀ b₁), (comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} P.Coefficient) T).mapDerivedCategory.map (DerivedCategory.Plus.ι.map D.etaleMap) ≫ b₁.comparison.hom = b₀.comparison.hom ≫ D.proEtaleMap) ∧ (∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} {b₀ b₁ : CompactSupportSiteBoundary P.Coefficient T} (D E : CompactSupportSiteDiagram P b₀ b₁), D.etaleMap = E.etaleMap → D.proEtaleMap = E.proEtaleMap)
